newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shilling eases further on importer demand.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shilling eases further on importer demand.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling weakened further on Tuesday fuelled by an increase in dollar demand from importers, commercial bank dealers said on Tuesday.
Kenya's central bank posted a commercial mean rate of 54.27 against the dollar from 54.14 on Monday, while against the pound, it was posted at a mean rate of 88.83 from 88.57.
"The shilling has suffered yet another blow today," a dealer said.
Dealers said importers had rushed into the market after holding out on the sidelines for the better part of last week to take advantage of the going rates.
"They've driven the shilling to 54.60/55," one dealer said.
However they added that dollar inflows expected from Tuesday's coffee auction could help stabilise the shilling.

At the moment, the market is particularly sensitive to any sudden movements in rates. What with a general election looming, foreign investors are already treading carefully -- a normal precaution in an election year, dealers said.
The money market remained liqiud with overnight rates quoted at eight percent, unchanged.
